idiom_name: struct implementing the repository trait over HashMap
implementation_notes: Rust has no reflection or code generation for working implementations, so the fake is a hand-written type implementing the same trait over a HashMap; when the trait takes &self, interior mutability (RefCell in single-threaded tests, Mutex or RwLock when the fake must be Send/Sync) is what lets writes be visible to later reads. Crates such as mockall generate mocks with expectations - the wrong tool when the test needs real behaviour. Keep the fake behind the same trait object or generic parameter the production code uses, and keep an integration test against the real adapter so trait drift is caught.
pitfalls: A RefCell borrow held across a call that re-enters the fake panics at runtime (already borrowed) - scope the borrow tightly or use a Mutex instead.
A fake behind #[cfg(test)] is invisible to integration tests in tests/, which are separate crates - put shared fakes in a test-support module or behind a feature.
Storing the fake in a static (OnceLock/LazyLock) shares it across tests and makes failures order-dependent; create a fresh instance per test.
